severity_basis: scored on the pattern, not the instance. The instance did no harm because an author re-derived from bytes; the pattern is that I hand-transformed source material twice in one wave and introduced an error both times.
what: building the class-sweep orders, I compressed the final checker's per-row evidence into one shared summary sentence and misattributed a site while doing it. The checker wrote, precisely: 'whole-token counts 5 and 1; the extra hits are eineinu (first plural) at 4.17 and 5.17 and mekhabbedeha (a different lexeme) at 1.8' - three extras spread across TWO citations. My order said the eye-form's extras were 'a first-PLURAL form and, at 1.8, a different lexeme', moving the 1.8 hit from the liver-form to the eye-form.
caught_by: fix author lam_fcfix_f06_a1, which re-derived both sweeps from the pointed text, found the extras were 4.17 and 5.17 for the eye-form and 1.8 for the liver-form, cured on the bytes it found, and wrote the discrepancy into its report rather than reproducing my illustration
why_no_harm: the brief tells an author to cure correctly and say why when the bytes disagree with a finding. It did exactly that. Both citations are correctly restated in rows_v14.

the_pattern_this_belongs_to.instance_1: the sweep launch messages pinned a corpus their orders did not name, because I built each launch by editing the previous one (finding_launch_orders_base_mismatch.v1.json)
the_pattern_this_belongs_to.instance_2: this one: the checker's evidence was paraphrased into a shared summary and an attribution moved
the_pattern_this_belongs_to.common_cause: both times I hand-transformed a source artifact instead of generating from it, and both times an author caught it rather than any check of mine

control: when an order generalises a class from sampled findings, the SOURCE residual is carried VERBATIM per row and any generalisation of mine is a separate, clearly-labelled field. An order may add my reasoning; it may not restate the evidence in my words, because a paraphrase of evidence is not evidence.
also_note: all three sweep authors independently reported the launch/orders corpus discrepancy and each explained how it handled it. That is three for three on the exact-path law doing its job.
authority: orchestrator self-report; candidate-only, non-authorizing; no corpus row is affected
